findings.title: Idle-clock unit guard is one-sided but documented as fail-closed
findings.why_it_matters: If `cpuInfo[].idleClock` is not microseconds on this console, CORE does not fall back to `--`. The only unit check is one-directional: `cpu_pct_from_idle()` rejects an idle delta that exceeds the elapsed time, so a counter that advances faster than wall time is caught, but a coarser counter (milliseconds, seconds, a tick larger than 1 us) passes, every per-core delta becomes a small fraction of elapsed, and the ratio renders a permanent ~100 % - the exact fabricated number D6/D103 forbid and the exact static-100 % symptom PROJECT.md's hardware checklist says must never appear, indistinguishable from a genuinely saturated machine. The stated intent for this change is to fail closed when the idle-clock unit is wrong, and four comments and docs promise a full guarantee the arithmetic does not provide. The two reviewers split on severity (P1 from project-standards against the intent contract, P2 from correctness because the unit itself is still [C] on hardware); the consequence if it is wrong is a fabricated hero number, so the cautious rating stands.

If it did, the unit is not microseconds ..." / if (idle > elapsed) { ... if (idle > elapsed + slack) return CPU_CORE_UNKNOWN; -- the only unit check in the tree, and it has no opposite-direction branch

vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:93-99 -- busy = 100.0 - idle*100/elapsed; a milliseconds counter yields 100 - 100*100/100000 = 99.9 %, rounded to 100 and clamped there.

findings.suggested_fix: Pick one and make code and docs agree. (a) Minimal: correct the guarantee in vita-cockpit/src/core/platform.h:83-85, vita-cockpit/src/platform/platform_psp2.c:165-166, vita-cockpit/docs/DECISIONS.md:1997 (D103), vita-cockpit/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:320, PROJECTS.md:26 and the metrics.c comment to say only a counter that advances faster than wall time is rejected, and add to PROJECT.md's hardware checklist: "a static ~100 % at idle means idleClock is coarser than microseconds; record it and treat CPU as unavailable". (b) Behavioural: also add the opposite-direction plausibility guard - if every active core reads exactly 100 % for five consecutive windows (0.5 s), refuse the sample and render `--` until the reading drops. Assumption: a false `--` is the safe direction under the project rule that a missing value beats a fabricated one.

findings.title: Fabricated CTX/WAKE 0/S when the cumulative counters are absent or regress
findings.why_it_matters: CORE prints `CTX 0/S  WAKE 0/S` as if it had measured them whenever the CPU sample is otherwise valid. `sample_cpu()` zeroes both rates at the top of every sample and then skips the assignment when a cumulative counter has not advanced or has gone backwards; `cpu_valid` is decided by the idle clocks alone, so the caption's only validity gate stays open. The adapter sums the two counters over the cores active at read time, so a narrowing `activeCpuMask` or a 32-bit `threadSwitchCount`/`comesOutOfIdleCount` wrap makes the total fall, and zero-filled or frozen counters from firmware that does not populate them read as a measured zero. On a running Vita zero context switches per second is impossible, so the hero panel shows an invented number - exactly the zero-substitution AGENTS.md rule 6, README.md:194 and the Metrics contract forbid. Three reviewers reached the same defect and fix path; the fix is the per-field validity pattern the POWER panel already uses.
evidence: vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:178-183 -- if (in.ctx_switches >= s_prev_cpu.ctx_switches) g_metrics.cpu_ctx_per_s = cpu_rate(...); (same for wakeups) -- when the test fails no assignment happens and no flag records it
vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:122-123 -- g_metrics.cpu_ctx_per_s = 0; g_metrics.cpu_wake_per_s = 0; re-seeded every sample, so the value left by a rejected delta is a plausible zero
vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:173 -- g_metrics.cpu_valid = 1; set from `cores > 0` alone, independent of whether either rate delta was accepted

findings.suggested_fix: Add `int cpu_ctx_valid; int cpu_wake_valid;` to the CPU block in Metrics, clear them with the other CPU fields at the top of sample_cpu(), set each only inside its `>=` branch, and have draw_caption() render `--` for whichever field is invalid (matching the per-field POWER pattern). Optionally mirror the `have_idle` gate in platform_read_cpu with a `have_counters` check if a fully absent pair should blank the whole row. Add zero, unchanged and backwards-counter cases to tools/test/test_metrics.c, and pin the shrinking-mask case.

findings.title: No test or preview renders the CPU fail-closed "--" path
findings.why_it_matters: The intent promises the panel falls back to "--" when the scheduler counters are missing or the idle-clock unit is wrong, but only the policy layer is asserted. If the per-core or caption fallback regressed (for example printing the zeroed percentage), every host check would still pass and no preview scene would reveal it, so the first evidence would come from the user's console run. The project already treats a fabricated number as worse than a missing one, which makes this the one display contract that should be proven before flashing.

findings.title: Docs place the idle-unit rejection in the adapter, not the policy
findings.why_it_matters: The `[C]` claim table exists so a hardware correction lands in the file its Where column names, and ARCHITECTURE.md:333 makes that promise explicit. This row says "the adapter rejects a delta larger than elapsed time" and points at `platform_psp2.c`, but `platform_read_cpu` contains no such check; the rejection is `cpu_pct_from_idle()` in `core/metrics.c`. A maintainer correcting the idle-clock unit after a console session would edit the adapter and leave the actual guard untouched, so the routing the document promises fails exactly when it is needed.

findings.title: Added CPU validity mask and CPU rate test hook have no consumer
findings.why_it_matters: The diff adds two pieces of CPU surface nothing consumes. `Metrics.cpu_active_mask` is written twice and read nowhere, and it records the candidate mask (`in.active_mask & s_prev_cpu.active_mask`) rather than the cores that actually produced a percentage, because the loop skips a core whose idle delta went backwards or failed the unit check - a later panel or test that trusts it would treat unmeasured cores as measured. `fake_set_cpu_activity()` is declared and defined but never called, so the fake advertises a rate knob nothing exercises while the rate assertions silently rely on `cpu_reset()`'s 840/230 defaults. AGENTS.md rule 9 forbids keeping code nothing invokes, and unused state on the shared Metrics contract invites exactly that kind of misuse.
evidence: vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.h:56 -- unsigned cpu_active_mask;
vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:121,174 -- g_metrics.cpu_active_mask = 0; / g_metrics.cpu_active_mask = mask; (two writes, no reader in src/ or tools/)

vita-cockpit/src/core/metrics.c:140,145 -- unsigned mask = in.active_mask & s_prev_cpu.active_mask; ... if ((mask & (1u << i)) == 0) continue; (the recorded mask is the candidate, not the measured set)
vita-cockpit/tools/fake/fake_platform.h:25 -- void fake_set_cpu_activity(int ctx_per_s, int wake_per_s);
vita-cockpit/tools/fake/fake_platform.c:137 -- void fake_set_cpu_activity(int ctx_per_s, int wake_per_s)  /* the only other match in the tree */
vita-cockpit/tools/test/test_metrics.c:87-88 -- CHECK(g_metrics.cpu_ctx_per_s == 840); CHECK(g_metrics.cpu_wake_per_s == 230); the rates are cpu_reset() defaults, not a value the test sets
AGENTS.md rule 9 -- "No dead code, no unused links. Do not link a library the source never calls. Do not keep a function nothing invokes."

findings.suggested_fix: Delete `Metrics.cpu_active_mask` and its two writes (metrics.c:121 and :174); per-core absence is already carried by CPU_CORE_UNKNOWN and the aggregate by cpu_valid. Delete `fake_set_cpu_activity` from tools/fake/fake_platform.h and fake_platform.c, or make it the only source of the tested rates by calling `fake_set_cpu_activity(900, 250)` in test_cpu_usage() and asserting 900/250. findings.title: PROJECTS.md Next cell lists three actions, not one
findings.why_it_matters: The board rule is that Next holds the single next action, but this row packs flash, CPU verification, and the remaining checklist into one semicolon chain. A board whose Next cells are checklists stops answering the question it exists for — what to do next — without re-reading the whole cell, and the superseded b150 row carried the same shape, so the pattern is spreading rather than being corrected. Collapsing the cell to the flash-and-confirm step and moving the rest of the checklist to Notes or the project doc restores the rule.
